Priority Planning Poker is a technique that allows everyone on the team to contribute to the prioritization process while removing bias equally.
Here are some benefits of using priority planning poker:
Gives everyone the option to contribute to the final priorities.
Highlights outside opinions to guide the discussion in the right direction.
Brings fun and gamifies the prioritization meetings.

attrs.alt: Example Priority Poker session.

content.text: How to play priority planning poker
The high-level steps of playing priority planning poker are:
Create a poker room with selected issues.
Everyone votes on metrics for selected issues in real-time.
Present the results of the voting, together with each member’s votes.
Discuss when necessary and accept the votes. Or re-take the voting if outliers are prominent.
Roles in the priority planning poker session
Everyone with Administer Foxly permission can create a poker session. When you create a session, you automatically become the Session admin.

pages.title: Get started with Foxly Project Prioritization

content.text: Foxly is a backlog prioritization app for Jira Cloud that helps managers and leads standardize how their team scores, ranks, and manages issues. Using customizable metrics and scoring formulas, Foxly gives every issue a calculated priority score — making it easier to align stakeholders and make data-driven prioritization decisions.
Customizable scoring formulas and prioritization metrics
Priority Matrix for visual quadrant-based issue management
Priority Planning Poker for collaborative team scoring
Saved views with shareable, project-level defaults
Prioritization history visible directly from issue details
Support for Jira custom fields as prioritization inputs
Async (offline) planning poker for distributed teams
Data residency options for EU, DE, AU, and US regions

A product team is struggling to align on which backlog items to tackle each sprint. Everyone has opinions, but there's no consistent way to compare items across different dimensions — customer impact, effort, and strategic value all matter, but they're being weighed differently by different people.

Using Foxly, the product manager creates a prioritization template with three metrics — Impact, Effort, and Confidence — and defines a weighted scoring formula. The team runs a Priority Planning Poker session to score the top 20 items together, then reviews the results in the Priority Matrix to identify which high-impact, low-effort issues should move to the top of the backlog.
The priority scores update automatically as metrics are adjusted, and the product manager saves a Default View so every team member lands on the same filtered, sorted table when they open Foxly.

The Saved Views feature allows users to quickly switch between views with a defined set of parameters, including:

The following enhancements are included in this release:
Share views from the address bar
The parametrized URL can now be shared with colleagues directly from the address bar.
Filters are persistent when switching from Matrix to Table
Filters no longer reset when navigating back to the Priority table from the Priority matrix.

When sorting the Priority table by Score, a Jira custom field, or a metric aligned with a custom field, sorting is now handled on the backend. This means the table loads faster and no longer has a 1,000-issue limit. Sorting by a metric not aligned with a Jira custom field retains the previous behavior.

This section covers how to get help with Foxly, including how to contact support, report a bug, or submit a feature request. You can also find information about data residency, permissions, and other administrative topics.
Foxly is a backlog prioritization app for Jira Cloud that allows managers and leads to standardize the backlog prioritization process using data metrics and scoring formulas.
Foxly keeps your team and stakeholders up to date on work priorities with real-time priority scoring.
Watch the Foxly getting started video!

Project issues appear in the table view together with metrics and the priority score. Click the fields to assign metrics to issues. Once all metrics are filled in for an issue, the score is automatically calculated.

Foxly now offers data residency options. Data residency gives you control over where your in-scope end-user data is hosted, allowing you to choose a defined geographic location.
The data residency option available for Foxly serves to:
Help ensure compliance with local data protection laws.
Enhance security by storing data within specific jurisdictions.
Provide users with greater control over their personal information, reducing legal risks.

With recent Atlassian API changes, you may encounter the following limitations when working with Jira custom fields.
If you add Jira custom fields to the view, their values will appear empty. This happens because the custom fields aren’t included in the relevant Jira screen.

attrs.alt: Screenshot of adding a field to the column view in Foxly.

content.text: If you’re using a prioritization template with metrics linked to Jira fields, the priority score won’t be calculated unless those fields are added to appropriate Jira screens.
, you can check what prioritization template is in use and see if metrics are based on Jira fields.

attrs.alt: Screenshot of the Configuration page in Foxly.

content.text: To resolve the above limitations, add the required fields to the appropriate Jira screens. See full instructions in the
Add a field to a screen
If you can’t access Jira settings, contact your Jira admin.
Once the necessary fields are added to Jira screens:
The values of Jira fields added to the column view will be visible.
The priority score will be calculated when a prioritization template based on Jira fields is in use.

pages.title: Use Jira custom fields with historical values

content.text: If you decide to use Jira custom fields in prioritization formulas as a replacement for existing prioritization metrics, you may want to preserve the historical values in those custom fields. This can be achieved by exporting data from Foxly and importing it into Jira using Jira’s import functionality.
Create custom fields in Jira that mirror the priority metrics (e.g., an Ease custom field).
